title: Artificial Intelligence and GenAI

maps.tested: Two full readings, both rated Very Important, and six recall sources. Counts of 2-3 questions per sitting are reported.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'AI (2-3)'; 'GEN AI 2 Qs'; 'AI vs Gen AI', an explicit discrimination question between the two; 'disadvantage of GenAI'; 'application of AI in market risk'. The AI-vs-GenAI split and the financial-stability implications (herding, model monoculture, third-party concentration, explainability) are the two examinable axes.

vardeezReading: CI-1: Very Important, "Please Solve Book Wise Current Issues Questions as anything can show up". CI-2: Very Important, "Solve book-wise Current Issues questions; anything can show up."

selectors.name: AI vs GenAI, model groups, hallucination
selectors.what: Tells AI/ML from GenAI: the IMF's established group (NLP, neural networks, decision trees, clustering) against the sophisticated group (LLMs, deep learning, reinforcement learning); what GenAI adds (Transformer architecture, LLM chatbots, idea generation, code for analysts); its signature failure mode, hallucination (a confident but incorrect output); and the human in the loop who still makes the final trading decision.

selectors.name: Disadvantages of GenAI
selectors.what: The downsides of GenAI: fraud and deepfakes (fake profiles, IDs, bypassed security checks), scalable disinformation, more frequent cyber attacks with lower entry barriers, the attack vectors prompt injection (extracts confidential information) and model or data poisoning (manipulates weights or training data), and bad actors gaining more than legitimate users in the short term.

selectors.name: Application of AI in market risk
selectors.what: How AI is used in market risk and risk management: volatility and liquidity risk models that predict how heightened volatility affects positions, advanced risk scenarios, tailored risk insights, compliance monitoring and dynamic risk sensing.

selectors.name: Financial stability: herding, concentration, explainability
selectors.what: Financial-stability vulnerabilities of AI: correlated models and herding (flash crashes, liquidity crunches, higher when LLMs inform risk management or strategy, lower for back-office uses), third-party and service-provider concentration with what pushes it up or down, and model risk with lack of explainability, data quality and governance within the institution's existing model risk framework.

notSelected: CI-1 b (market dynamics), CI-1 d (regulators and supervisors), CI-2 b (industry and supervisory use cases beyond market risk) and the supply-side and demand-side drivers of CI-2 a, and the cyber, fraud and misalignment items beyond those named in S2 and S4, carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer beyond the general advice to solve the book-wise questions.
